messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] nancycat dataset
parts:
Hello Sam,

eMLG, H, G, lambda, and E.5 all measure diversity of multilocus genotypes (MLG). If N = MLG, then all genotypes are equally rare which drives these diversity measures to their maximum value (for H, that's log(N)). This is important for assessing population structure in a clonal organism, but not so much in one that reproduces sexually (like cats). 

Hope that answers your question :)

Best,
Zhian

-----

Postdoctoral Researcher (Everhart Lab)

Thanks Zhian for your reply, i agree that it is not informative for non-clonal organisms when trying to measure shannon's in this way. What i actually want is to measure Shannon's based on alleles rather than multilocus genotypes, in that for each population an average Shannon's per locus is generated. The mean output of the locus_table() in poppr is exactly what i am looking for  So I am wondering if there is a function that generates a list of average Shannon's per locus (or even Simpson's) for each population that is based on allelic data?

Cheers,
Sam

Hi Samantha,

I'm afraid it's a bit of roll-your-own at the moment. There is functionality to generate resampled data in the 'mmod' package (function: chao_bootstrap), but that's where the baked-in functions end. You can take the bootstrap samples and map the statistics on to them just like they were mapped to the separated populations in the script attached previously. 

I hope that helps,
Zhian

On Monday, 5 February 2018 11:35:42 UTC+11, Zhian Kamvar wrote:
Hi Samantha,

I'm afraid it's a bit of roll-your-own at the moment. There is functionality to generate resampled data in the 'mmod' package (function: chao_bootstrap), but that's where the baked-in functions end. You can take the bootstrap samples and map the statistics on to them just like they were mapped to the separated populations in the script attached previously. 

I hope that helps,
Zhian

On Feb 4, 2018, at 17:20 , Samantha Yap <syap...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thank you Zhian, that was very helpful. However, there is also the problem of uneven sampling of the populations in my dataset. Just curious, there isn't a built-in bootstrapping function for randomly drawing samples within a population, and then calculating confidence of the resampled allelic richness/other genetic indices, is there?

Cheers,
Sam 


On Saturday, 13 January 2018 03:02:06 UTC+11, Zhian Kamvar wrote:
Hi Sam,

There is no function that automates this, but because poppr is written in R, it IS possible to create a function that will extract the last row of the locus table and loop over all populations to give you a data frame with the results. I'm attaching an R script that illustrates this.

Best,
Zhian

On Jan 11, 2018, at 16:59 , Samantha Yap <syap...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thanks Zhian for your reply, i agree that it is not informative for non-clonal organisms when trying to measure shannon's in this way. What i actually want is to measure Shannon's based on alleles rather than multilocus genotypes, in that for each population an average Shannon's per locus is generated. The mean output of the locus_table() in poppr is exactly what i am looking for  So I am wondering if there is a function that generates a list of average Shannon's per locus (or even Simpson's) for each population that is based on allelic data?

Cheers,
Sam
